newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOST GRAINS FUTURES DOWN IN SLOW BUDAPEST MARKET.
newsitem.headline: MOST GRAINS FUTURES DOWN IN SLOW BUDAPEST MARKET.

text.p: Most grains futures prices of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) dropped on Wednesday with milling wheat making up the bulk of turnover, traders said.
"Extensive press reports of excess mill stocks of both wheat and wheat flour pushed the price of the old (1996) crop down" said Robert Vajo of Termin.
Milling wheat prices dropped by the daily allowed 400 forints limit for all maturities, ending between 24,700 forints per tonne for May and 23,000 forints for December.
Vajo added that a technical correction and the downward movement of the old crop was behind the new crop's price slump.
There was hardly any trade in maize futures, with only 20 contracts changing hands.
"There is a bearish mood about maize on the Hungarian market despite contrary international trends" Vajo said.
He added, however, that rising international prices and relatively good export prices to neighbouring countries could prevent or at least slow further falls.
Maize prices remained unchanged for most maturities, except for July which finished at 17,490 forints, down 10, and November which finished at 18,300, down 350.
Two new maturities, October and December, opened for feed barley, at 18,500 and 18,700 forints respectively.
Total turnover was a meagre 644 lots or 291.4 million forints, of which 525 were for milling wheat.
